description: Proj. ENZYLA is the official and recognized team of aspiring students from Batch Stellarius of Naga City Science High School, representing the school in this hackathon. Focusing on CLPS Lunar Browser, the team aims to enhance its capabilities, design, and user experience through innovative features and creative solutions. Driven by curiosity, collaboration, and ambition, Proj. ENZYLA seeks to transform Lunar Browser into a more powerful, intuitive, and distinctive platform while showcasing the ingenuity of young Filipino innovators.
summary: Project ENZYLA is an advanced lunar navigation and geospatial analysis system designed to enhance the computational capabilities, functionality, and user experience of existing lunar browser platforms. It integrates an interactive artificial intelligence model that facilitates real-time data monitoring, interpretation, and comparative analysis of lunar geographical features. By processing geospatial coordinates, including latitude and longitude, alongside Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) datasets, the AI model assists users in identifying, visualizing, and evaluating potential lunar landing sites based on their geographical and topographical characteristics. Furthermore, its self-diagnostic functionality enables the system to detect, assess, and identify potential software anomalies, improving operational reliability and data-processing efficiency. Through the integration of AI-assisted geospatial interpretation, interactive data visualization, and automated system diagnostics, Project ENZYLA provides a more comprehensive and data-driven platform for lunar terrain exploration, landing site assessment, and future mission planning.
details:
Project ENZYLA

ENZYLA is an interactive platform for lunar exploration and analysis, designed to make the Moon's surface, its geology, and its potential landing sites more accessible and comprehensible. It brings together 3D visualization, scientific data, and AI to create an engaging environment in which to explore and compare potential landing sites.

The platform works by taking NASA's existing 3d lunar visualization model and populating it with the relevant lunar geology and topography. Users can then go in and explore the Moon, look at the surface, look at the features, and assess how those features might impact the suitability of a landing site. ENZYLA is attempting to strike a balance between scientific accuracy, accessibility, and performance so that both the novice and the technically minded user can interact with the complex data.

One of its key features is D.A.R.Y.L. (Dynamic Artificial Reasoning & Yielding Liaison), which is an AI assistant that is integrated into the system to guide you through your experience. D.A.R.Y.L. can cater to users of all levels of technical know-how, from answering the very general questions of a typical visitor right through to assisting with more sophisticated queries from students, researchers, engineers, and other scientists.

The project has a number of advantages. It makes the lunar geology much more interactive and accessible, provides a visual means of looking at potential landing sites, and is a great way of stimulating scientific interest and the desire to explore. It brings together the power of visualization with AI-assisted guidance in order to lower the barrier between the complex science and the public.

Its aim is to help make lunar exploration more accessible and informed. It's about providing geographical information in an interactive 3D environment to support education, scientific research, and the planning of future lunar missions. ENZYLA's ultimate goal is to make space science more accessible and to stimulate interest in planetary science and space exploration.

For development we're using HTML, CSS and JavaScript with Node.js as our development environment and to provide the various bits of functionality. Tailwind CSS is used for the styling of the interface and Three.js/WebGL for the 3d rendering and interactive visualization. The basis of the lunar visualization is NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS) lunar model (specifically SVS 14959). We're also using lunar topography and heightmap integration as part of the effort to get the surface representation right. D.A.R.Y.L. is the project's in-built AI.

What makes ENZYLA creative is the way it combines a number of technologies into one experience. Instead of just giving you a map of the Moon, a series of static images, or a set of disparate data sets, it brings together an interactive 3D environment, scientific geographical data, and an AI assistant. You can explore, you can learn, and you can ask questions all within the same experience.

Throughout the development process a number of key issues were considered: scientific accuracy, data quality, geographical registration, visual quality, performance of the application, accessibility, and usability. A significant balance was struck between the level of topographic detail and the computational cost of that detail, with the aim of ensuring that the platform remains responsive without at the same time being excessively 'detailed.' The needs of different user groups were also taken into account in the design of the experience, with the intention of making it work for both the novice and the more technically adept user.

Through ENZYLA we're hoping to show how accessible technology, scientific data and AI can come together to create new opportunities for understanding and exploring our closest neighbor in the solar system.
